name: Preservation Hall
unique: A 200-person room with no air conditioning, no drinks and no amplification, where the oldest generation of New Orleans jazz musicians still plays nightly.
buzz: The line forms early and the room is a sauna; everyone says it is the best hour in the city. Buy the seated tickets if you can.

name: The National WWII Museum
unique: A vast museum with a restored Higgins boat, a Sherman tank, a 4D theater and the personal stories of the war in Europe and the Pacific.
buzz: One of the best museums in the country, and it takes most of a day. Start with the film and the train car.

name: New Orleans Jazz Fest
company: New Orleans Jazz and Heritage Festival
unique: Twelve stages of jazz, gospel, zydeco and rock, plus a food fair of crawfish monica, cochon de lait and mango freeze that rivals the music.
buzz: The food is half the reason to go; crowds are enormous and the walk from parking is long. Locals go early and leave before dark.

name: Mardi Gras
unique: Weeks of parades built by private krewes, with floats, brass bands, beads and a social order that goes back generations.
buzz: Go to the uptown parades, not just Bourbon Street; locals are welcoming if you respect the routes. Book lodging months ahead.

name: 13th Gate Escape
unique: Escape rooms built by the team behind one of the country's top haunted houses, with cinematic sets, live actors and puzzles that lean into horror rather than padlocks.
buzz: Escape enthusiasts rank it among the best in the country; the sets are film quality and the scares are real. Book the hardest room if you are experienced.

name: Crawfish Boil Season
unique: A backyard ritual elevated to civic religion: a propane burner, a 100-quart pot, crawfish, corn, potatoes and a table covered in newspaper.
buzz: The best boils are at someone's house; Breaux Bridge in spring is the fallback. Learn to peel or go hungry.

name: Frenchmen Street
unique: A strip of live music clubs, bars and restaurants just outside the French Quarter, where locals go to hear brass, funk and jazz.
buzz: The clubs are close together and the cover charges are low. Start early and follow your ears.

name: 13th Gate Haunted House
customer: Haunted house fans, teens, young adults
unique: A seasonal haunted attraction with movie grade sets, a crematorium, a swamp and thirty plus scenes, regularly ranked among the best in the United States.
buzz: The detail is the difference: real props, trained actors and a route that keeps moving. Buy the fast pass if you hate lines.

name: City Park
unique: A 1,300 acre park with live oaks, a sculpture garden, a children's amusement park, a botanical garden and paddle boats on a lagoon.
buzz: The sculpture garden is free and the oaks are magnificent. Rent a bike or a boat.

name: Honey Island Swamp Tour
company: Dr. Wagner's Honey Island Swamp Tours
unique: A small boat into a cypress swamp with wild alligators, barred owls and a trapper's camp, guided by people who live on the water.
buzz: Small boats beat the big airboats for wildlife; guides are funny and knowledgeable. Bring bug spray and a zoom lens.

name: The Myrtles
unique: A 1796 plantation house with a famous haunted history, offering mystery tours, a restaurant and overnight stays in rooms where guests report footsteps and mirrors that move.
buzz: The house and grounds are beautiful and the ghost stories are well told; overnight guests either love it or check out early. Book the tour even if you skip the stay.

name: Angola Prison Rodeo
unique: Inmates ride bulls and compete in poker-on-horseback inside a maximum-security prison, with a craft fair of prison-made goods and a crowd of thousands.
buzz: People call it the most complicated day of their trip, spectacle, exploitation and genuine skill all at once. Tickets sell out.

name: St. Louis Cemetery No. 1
unique: The oldest cemetery in the city, with above ground tombs, the grave of Marie Laveau and a maze of family vaults.
buzz: You can only enter with a guide now, and the history of the burial customs is the point. Book ahead.

name: Vermilionville
unique: A living history village of Acadian, Creole and Native American houses on the bayou, with music, cooking and craft demonstrations.
buzz: The music and food demos are the best part, and the village is shady and walkable. Good for kids.

name: Oak Alley Plantation
unique: A quarter mile avenue of 300-year old live oaks leading to a Greek Revival mansion, with the slave quarters and sugar operation interpreted alongside the beauty.
buzz: The grounds are stunning and the slavery exhibits are more honest than most; the mint julep is a nice touch. Go early for photos.

name: Avery Island Tabasco Tour
unique: The pepper sauce aged in white oak barrels on a salt dome, with a museum, a jungle garden of camellias and a walk where you can see the barrels sweating.
buzz: Cheap, quirky and genuinely interesting; the gardens are a surprise. The tasting room lets you try the family's reserve sauce.

name: LSU Rural Life Museum
unique: A 450 acre museum of Louisiana rural life with a plantation complex, slave cabins, a country store and farm equipment.
buzz: The slave cabins and the working farm are the powerful parts. The grounds are shady and quiet.

name: Madewood Plantation
unique: A Greek Revival mansion on Bayou Lafourche, still family owned and open for tours and overnight stays.
buzz: The house is stunning and the family story is personal. Book ahead for a tour or a night.

name: Natchitoches Historic District
unique: The oldest settlement in Louisiana, with a brick main street, a river walk, a fort site and 18th century houses.
buzz: The river street is the photo and the meat pies are the local food. Christmas lights are a big draw.

name: USS Kidd
unique: A World War II destroyer docked on the Mississippi, restored and open for self guided tours through the decks and turrets.
buzz: The ship is tight and real, and the museum explains the Pacific war. Good for kids who like machines.

name: Middendorf's
unique: A roadhouse on a swamp pass between two lakes, famous for thin fried catfish and a view of the Manchac swamp from the dining room windows.
buzz: The thin catfish is the order and the swamp view is the setting; it is a detour people make on purpose. Cash for the tip jar.

name: Louisiana State Capitol
unique: The tallest state capitol in the country, with an Art Deco interior, a observation deck and the spot where Huey Long was shot.
buzz: The observation deck view is the reason, and the building is a monument to Long's ambition. Free.

name: Mardi Gras World
unique: The warehouse where parade floats are built, with giant figures, props and a tour through the painting and sculpting shops.
buzz: The scale of the floats is the fun and kids love it. The tour includes a slice of king cake.

name: Natchitoches Christmas Lights
unique: Three hundred thousand lights along a 33-block historic riverfront, with boat parades, fireworks and meat pies, the oldest holiday light display in the South.
buzz: It is a genuine small town spectacle; parking is the challenge. Eat a Natchitoches meat pie while you walk.

name: Abita Brewing
unique: The oldest craft brewery in the South, in a piney town across Lake Pontchartrain, with a tour, a tasting room and a brewpub pouring seasonals you cannot get elsewhere.
buzz: The tour is casual and generous; the purple haze and the root beer are the local favorites. A good rainy day in New Orleans.

name: Abbeville Shrimp Festival
unique: A street festival in the shrimp capital of Louisiana, with boiled shrimp, gumbo, music and a parade.
buzz: The food is the point and the shrimp are fresh. Go early for parking.

name: Southdown Plantation
unique: A 1859 sugar plantation house with a museum of the sugar industry, the enslaved workers and the Cajun culture that followed.
buzz: The sugar history is well told and the house is handsome. Check hours before driving out.

name: Biedenharn Museum and Gardens
unique: The home of the first bottler of Coca-Cola, with the original bottling plant, a museum and formal gardens.
buzz: The bottling equipment and the family story are the interesting parts. The gardens are a bonus.

name: Brownell Memorial Park
unique: A small park with a 100 foot observation tower, a cypress swamp and a rookery full of egrets and herons.
buzz: The tower gives a canopy view of the swamp and the birds are close. Free.

name: Los Islenos Museum
unique: A museum of the Canary Islanders who settled the parish in the 1770s, with a village, a church and the story of the 2005 flood.
buzz: The Isleno history is unique and the flood exhibit is moving. Free.

name: Sci-Port Discovery Center
unique: A hands on science center with a planetarium, an IMAX, a space exhibit and a toddler area on the Shreveport riverfront.
buzz: Good for a rainy day with kids, with enough to fill an afternoon. The planetarium is a bonus.

name: Fort Jackson
unique: A brick fort on the Mississippi below New Orleans, used in the Civil War and later as a prison, with a moat and a river view.
buzz: The fort is weathered and quiet, and the river is right there. A good stop on the way to the delta.
